title: Sell Mineral Rights in Kenmar, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Kenmar, PA
metaDescription: Kenmar is a small Lycoming County community in the dry-gas Marcellus core. See how inherited fractional interests here get evaluated fairly.
heroLead: Kenmar is a small unincorporated community in Lycoming County, tucked inside dry-gas Marcellus territory that's been drilled steadily for over a decade.
intro: Small communities like Kenmar don't show up on many maps, but the mineral interests underneath them show up plenty in county records, usually split among heirs who scattered to different states after the farm was sold off or passed down. If you inherited a piece of a Kenmar-area interest and the only mail you get about it is an occasional letter from a landman, you're not alone — that's the normal state of affairs for a lot of rural Lycoming acreage.

sections.heading: Why So Many Kenmar Interests Are Fractional
paragraphs: Rural land around Kenmar tended to stay in single families for generations, which sounds simple until that family grows to four or five branches, each inheriting an equal fractional share of the same mineral interest. None of those heirs individually owns enough to make a major decision alone, but together the whole interest can still be leased or sold as a unit if everyone's willing.

It also helps to know that a lot of the paperwork around Kenmar interests never made it past a handshake generations ago, which is exactly why we lean on the recorded deed rather than family memory when we start a file.

sections.heading: Lycoming's Dry-Gas Track Record
paragraphs: Lycoming County has been one of the more consistently drilled dry-gas counties in the Marcellus play, and that history means there's usually real production and royalty data nearby to work from, rather than pure speculation about what a well might someday produce.

sections.heading: Getting All the Heirs on the Same Page
paragraphs: We've walked plenty of families through the process of coordinating a sale among multiple heirs, including tracking down cousins who moved out of state and haven't thought about the family mineral interest in years. It takes patience, but it's routine, not rare.

faqs.question: I only own a small fraction — is it worth pursuing?
faqs.answer: Small fractional interests are the norm around Kenmar given how many generations these tracts have passed through, and it's still worth getting a real evaluation.

faqs.question: What if some heirs want to sell and others don't?
faqs.answer: Each heir can generally decide separately for their own share; we can work with whoever is ready while leaving others out of the transaction.

faqs.question: How do you find current royalty history for a Kenmar tract?
faqs.answer: Through recorded division orders and unit filings at the Lycoming County courthouse, plus operator-reported production data where available.

faqs.question: Does Kenmar show up on maps at all?
faqs.answer: It's small enough that many maps skip it, but the Lycoming County tax and deed records name it specifically, which is all that matters for confirming ownership.
